title: The stable core of a submodule of a flat coalgebra comodule
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Let $C$ be an $R$-module flat over $R$, meaning that tensoring with $C$ preserves injections of $R$-modules, with $R$-linear maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_R C$ and $\epsilon:C\to R$ satisfying coassociativity and both counit identities. Tensor products have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Let $M$ be an $R$-module with an $R$-linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_R C$ satisfying $(\rho\otimes1_C)\rho=(1_M\otimes\Delta)\rho$ and $(1_M\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$, under the canonical associativity and unit identifications. For an $R$-submodule $W\subseteq M$, write $i_W:W\hookrightarrow M$ and define $W^\circ=\{m\in M:\rho(m)\in\operatorname{im}(i_W\otimes1_C)\}$. Then $W^\circ$ is an $R$-submodule contained in $W$. Writing $j:W^\circ\hookrightarrow M$, there is a unique $R$-linear map $\rho_\circ:W^\circ\to W^\circ\otimes_R C$ with $(j\otimes1_C)\rho_\circ=\rho j$; it satisfies $(\rho_\circ\otimes1_C)\rho_\circ=(1_{W^\circ}\otimes\Delta)\rho_\circ$ and $(1_{W^\circ}\otimes\epsilon)\rho_\circ=1_{W^\circ}$. Moreover, every $R$-submodule $U\subseteq W$ satisfying $\rho(U)\subseteq\operatorname{im}(i_U\otimes1_C)$ is contained in $W^\circ$, where $i_U:U\hookrightarrow M$. No Noetherian, finite generation, or torsion-freeness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Milne, Basic Theory of Affine Group Schemes (2012), VIII, Aside 4.7, printed p.117 (PDF p.117), the stable-core lemma preceding the finite-generation argument. Read https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/AGS.pdf; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $K=W^\circ$. The image of $i_W\otimes1_C$ is a submodule, so its inverse image under the linear map $\rho$ is a submodule. If $k\in K$, write $\rho(k)=\sum_a w_a\otimes c_a$ with $w_a\in W$. Applying $1_M\otimes\epsilon$ gives $k=\sum_a\epsilon(c_a)w_a\in W$ by counitality. Thus $K\subseteq W$.

source.place: Agent completion of Milne VIII Aside 4.7, stable-core lemma; tensor universal property and pure-tensor generation, Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: Let $q:M\to M/W$ be the quotient map and set $f=(q\otimes1_C)\rho:M\to(M/W)\otimes_R C$. The quotient sequence $W\xrightarrow{i_W}M\xrightarrow q M/W\to0$ is exact: $q$ is surjective and its kernel is $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], $\ker(q\otimes1_C)=\operatorname{im}(i_W\otimes1_C)$, so $K=\ker f$.

source.place: Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, applied to the quotient sequence.

proof.text: For $k\in K$, coassociativity gives, under associativity identifications, $((f\otimes1_C)\rho)(k)=(q\otimes1_C\otimes1_C)(\rho\otimes1_C)\rho(k)=(q\otimes1_C\otimes1_C)(1_M\otimes\Delta)\rho(k)=(1_{M/W}\otimes\Delta)f(k)=0$. The penultimate equality holds on every pure tensor and hence on their span. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with the flat module $C$ to the exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow j M\xrightarrow f(M/W)\otimes_R C$. Thus $j\otimes1_C$ is injective with image $\ker(f\otimes1_C)$, which contains $\rho(K)$ by the calculation. For each $k$ there is therefore exactly one $\rho_\circ(k)\in K\otimes_R C$ mapping to $\rho(k)$. Injectivity and linearity of $\rho$ imply that this assignment is linear (compare images of sums and scalar multiples); the same injectivity proves uniqueness of the linear map.

source.place: Agent coassociativity calculation completing Milne VIII Aside 4.7; Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), with Tag 00HB (definition-flat), for tensor preservation of the kernel sequence.

proof.text: To check counitality, postcompose $(1_K\otimes\epsilon)\rho_\circ$ with the injection $j$: its composite is $(1_M\otimes\epsilon)\rho j=j$, so it equals $1_K$. For coassociativity postcompose both sides with $j\otimes1_C\otimes1_C$, which is injective by applying [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] twice to an injection and the flat module $C$. The two composites are $(\rho\otimes1_C)\rho j$ and $(1_M\otimes\Delta)\rho j$, respectively, by $(j\otimes1_C)\rho_\circ=\rho j$ and functoriality of tensor on pure tensors. They agree by coassociativity on $M$. Cancel the injection.

source.place: Agent verification of the restricted coaction identities; Tag 00HD (lemma-flat) for the two tensor injections, and Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) for functoriality.

proof.text: Finally, let $U\subseteq W$ satisfy the stated stability condition. The inclusion $i_U:U\to M$ factors through $i_W$, hence $\operatorname{im}(i_U\otimes1_C)\subseteq\operatorname{im}(i_W\otimes1_C)$ by tensor functoriality. For $u\in U$, stability puts $\rho(u)$ in the first image, hence in the second; the definition of $K$ gives $u\in K$. This proves maximality.

source.place: Agent maximality argument for Milne VIII Aside 4.7; tensor functoriality from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).
